Cambodia's exports reached $17.09 billion in the first half (H1) this year—a 19.5-per cent YoY rise, official statistics show. 
The US was the largest export market during the six-month period, with shipments valued at $7.17 billion, accounting for more than 42 per cent of total exports. 
The country imported goods worth $19.76 billion during the period—an increase of 21.4 per cent YoY.

title: CDC, JDI discuss Cambodia-Japan SEZ master plan
summary:
The Council for the Development of Cambodia recently discussed with the Japan Development Institute formulation of an international-standard master plan for the Cambodia-Japan Special Economic Zone. 
The project aims at enhancing Cambodia’s attractiveness to support the supply chains of Japanese investors and businesses in the country, Cambodian Deputy PM Sun Chanthol said.

title: Dhaka to raise cash incentive for RMG exports made with domestic yarn
summary:
Bangladesh will raise the cash incentive for apparel exports made with locally-produced yarn from 1.5 per cent to 5 per cent, the finance minister has said. 
The move would cost the exchequer nearly $308 million. 
Garment exporters earlier received a 4-per cent cash incentive for using domestic yarn, but it was cut to 1.5 per cent in 2024 as part of preparations for graduation from the LDC status.

title: Textile focus of China’s 2026-2030 Five-Year Plan signals capacity war
summary:
China’s 15th Five-Year Plan aims to expand textile capacity despite a ~30 per cent fall in US import prices since 2019. 
US Section 301 cases propose 10-12.5 per cent textile duties plus a US-input incentive before end-2026. 
China+1 remains exposed: Bangladesh sourced 58.3 per cent of textiles and 87.4 per cent of knitted fabrics from China in Q1 2026.

title: Vietnam needs to do more to maintain H2 2026 export momentum: Experts
summary:
Vietnam needs more efforts to maintain export growth momentum in H2 2026 as despite encouraging performance, exports heavily depend on limited markets and product groups, while many export items reply on imported raw materials, experts say. 
Subdued consumption in major markets, falling commodity prices, growing trade barriers and high global interest rates would continue to weigh on export performance.

title: US fabric test material aims to improve textile recycling
summary:
The US National Institute of Standards and Technology has developed RGTM 10279 to assess fibre-identification methods used in textile sorting. 
The five-fabric test material can help recycling centres, labs and manufacturers validate NIR, computer vision and AI-enabled systems. 
For brands and sourcing teams, it may support fabric-composition checks before production and improve recovered.

title: US textile & apparel exports drop 8.8% in January-May 2026
summary:
US textile and apparel exports fell 8.87 per cent to $8.58 billion in January–May 2026, Office of Textiles and Apparel (OTEXA) data showed, as shipments to most key markets declined.
Yarn exports recorded the steepest drop, while apparel and fabric exports also weakened.
Falling exports to Mexico, China and Central America reflected softer regional manufacturing demand.

title: Germany's inflation eases further in June 2026: Destasis
summary:
Germany’s CPI inflation eased to 2.3 per cent year on year (YoY) in June 2026, with prices down 0.3 per cent from May, according to Destasis.
It said energy product prices slowed to a 3.4 per cent rise, easing some pressure on consumers. 
Its data showed core inflation above headline at 2.5 per cent and services up 3.1 per cent, keeping pricing signals for sourcing teams.

title: Why is Bangladesh’s apparel industry shedding jobs?
summary:
Bangladesh’s garment sector is reportedly facing factory closures and layoffs, leaving thousands jobless. 
Many workers, 20,000 as per some estimates, were reportedly affected in the first half of the year amid falling orders, rising costs and financing challenges facing the industry. 
The crisis underscores the sector’s struggle to balance global competitiveness with employment stability.

title: Jordan's apparel exports climb to $751 mn in January-April 2026
summary:
Jordan's apparel exports rose to 533.78 million JD in January–April 2026 from 518.86 million JD a year earlier, supported by strong shipments of knitted garments.
Total textile and apparel exports also climbed to 582.26 million JD, while apparel and overall textile imports recorded modest increases, reflecting resilient trade activity and sustained global demand for Jordanian products.

title: Can Bangladesh hold on to its EU edge after LDC graduation?
summary:
Bangladesh is reportedly simultaneously pursuing an EU free trade agreement and GSP Plus status to protect its exports as duty-free access ends after LDC graduation. 
With the EU buying nearly half its exports, delays in an FTA and stronger competition from India and Vietnam, stakeholders believe, could erode the country’s hard-won edge in its biggest market.

title: Amazon-AEPC’s $80 bn goal rewires India’s apparel exports
summary:
Amazon's $80 bn export goal arrives as US tariff changes weaken China’s direct-to-consumer advantage, giving Indian apparel MSMEs a rare opportunity to expand through marketplace exports.  
The opportunity may be short-lived. Section 122 expiry and ongoing US legal challenges could quickly alter India’s tariff advantage, making faster exporter onboarding and pricing discipline critical.

title: India amends footwear QCOs to ease compliance
summary:
India has amended two footwear Quality Control Orders for leather, rubber, polymeric and other footwear and components.
The legacy stock clearance deadline moves to July 31, 2027, giving manufacturers, distributors and retailers more time to liquidate inventory.
Footwear makers may import up to 4,500 sample pairs annually for R&D, subject to non-sale and record rules.

title: India exports $177 mn; may make 90% of luxury embroidery—no credit
summary:
India’s embroidery exports are expanding rapidly, with over one-third shipped to Italy and France, underscoring its key role in luxury fashion supply chains.
Yet customs origin rules often credit only the final manufacturing country.
As traceability evolves, recognising craftsmanship alongside manufacturing could become a new source of value in global fashion.

title: Why did 830 Italian leather firms close while luxury prices stay high?
summary:
Italy’s apparel exports continue to grow, but Florence’s fashion manufacturing base is shrinking as workshops close and skilled jobs disappear.
The gap highlights how rising export values do not necessarily sustain suppliers.
Long-term competitiveness depends on ensuring more value reaches manufacturers, protecting specialist skills and strengthening resilient local production.

title: US T&A imports drop to $39 bn in Jan-May; Vietnam retains top spot
summary:
US textile and apparel imports fell 8.92 per cent to $39.13 billion in January-May 2026, according to the Office of Textiles and Apparel (OTEXA).
Vietnam remained the top supplier, while China's shipments declined sharply.
Apparel and non-apparel imports both weakened, reflecting shifting sourcing towards Southeast Asia amid tariff concerns and changing supply chain strategies.

title: US' Carter’s reports 86% sustainable cotton sourcing in 2025
summary:
Carter’s has released its annual Raise the Future Impact Report for 2025, informing about progress in its sustainability commitments. 
The report says over 86 per cent of 2025 cotton was BCI Cotton or organic, with over 60 per cent of sales tied to responsible cotton. 
It cut virgin plastic packaging 90 per cent from 2022, reached 90 per cent recycled content, and expanded takeback and recycling pilots.

title: US' Authentic names Experience Group as Lee's Europe partner
summary:
Authentic Brands Group has announced a long-term partnership with Experience Group for Lee across Europe, tied to its planned acquisition of the denim brand. 
Experience Group will operate Lee in Europe across menswear and womenswear sportswear, activewear and workwear. 
The agreement targets wholesale, retail and e-commerce growth after the acquisition closes in the second half of 2026.
